figures.finding: A child under fifteen may be employed in public entertainment or information through cinema, theatre, radio, television or other media where that is essential, under a contract the parents conclude with the child's agreement and the Department of Labor and Employment's approval, and only after the employer secures a DOLE work permit; under fifteen the child works at most 4 hours a day and 20 a week and never 20:00-06:00; from fifteen to eighteen at most 8 hours a day and 40 a week, never 22:00-06:00.

value.permit: DOLE work permit, secured by the employer before engaging the child
value.reachesWritingDirecting: the exception names employment or participation in public entertainment or information through media, not only performing

figures.applies: Philippines, RA 7610 ss. 12, 12-A as amended by RA 9231.

sources.said: Where a child's employment or participation in public entertainment or information through cinema, theater, radio, television or other forms of media is essential: Provided , That the employment contract is concluded by the child's parents or legal guardian, with the express agreement of the child concerned, if possible, and the approval of the Department of Labor and Employment
the employer shall first secure, before engaging such child, a work permit from the Department of Labor and Employment
A child below fifteen (15) years of age may be allowed to work for not more than twenty (20) hours a week: Provided , That the work shall not be more than four (4) hours at any given day
A child fifteen (15) years of age but below eighteen (18) shall not be allowed to work for more than eight (8) hours a day, and in no case beyond forty (40) hours a week

No child below fifteen (15) years of age shall be allowed to work between eight o'clock in the evening and six o'clock in the morning of the following day and no child fifteen (15) years of age but below eighteen (18) shall be allowed to work between ten o'clock in the evening and six o'clock in the morning

figures.finding: A working child's income is his own, at most 20% may go to the family's needs, and where it reaches ₱200,000 a year the parents must put at least 30% in a trust fund, accounted to DOLE twice a year, which the child controls at majority (eighteen).

value.contractBy: parents or legal guardian, with the child's express agreement if possible, DOLE approval

setAside.into: trust fund set up by the parent or guardian

figures.applies: Philippines, RA 7610 ss. 12-B, 12-C as added by RA 9231; majority RA 6809.

sources.said: not more than twenty percent (20%) of the child's income may be used for the collective needs of the family

The parent or legal guardian of a working child below eighteen (18) years of age shall set up a trust fund for at least thirty percent (30%) of the earnings of the child whose wages and salaries from work and other income amount to at least two hundred thousand pesos (P200,000.00) annually, for which he/she shall render a semi-annual accounting of the fund to the Department of Labor and Employment
The child shall have full control over the trust fund upon reaching the age of majority.

figures.finding: Natural persons who incorporate a Philippine corporation (including a One Person Corporation) must be of legal age, eighteen.
figures.applies: Philippines, Revised Corporation Code (RA 11232) s. 10; majority RA 6809.

sources.said: Incorporators who are natural persons must be of legal age.
